caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
debt_management: Sudan's debt is among the world's highest and mostly in arrears. From 53.7% of GDP in 2007 it climbed as oil revenues were lost with South Sudan's secession (2011) and the government borrowed to fund deficits: 278.8% in 2020, the series high, easing to a projected 188.1% in 2025 largely through denominator and exchange-rate effects rather than repayment. Sudan reached the HIPC decision point in 2021, which promised eventual relief, but the 2021 coup and 2023 war froze the process. Most external debt is in arrears to bilateral and multilateral creditors; the numbers describe a debt stock that cannot and will not be serviced without a political settlement and full HIPC completion.
inflation_management: Sudan's inflation is a chronicle of state failure. It was contained at 7-18% through 2011, then the loss of oil revenues and money-printing drove it to 35-37% in 2012-2014. The 2019 revolution's aftermath brought 51.0% in 2019, then full collapse: 163.3% in 2020 and a series high of 359.1% in 2021 as the pound was devalued and deficits monetized. Brief stabilization (77.2% in 2023) ended with the war: 185.7% in 2024 and 100.2% projected for 2025. The central bank is split and dysfunctional; inflation is driven by war finance, and there is no monetary framework to speak of.

key_events.event: South Sudan's secession cost Sudan most of its oil revenues; GDP peaked at $66.5bn (2011).
Protests ousted Omar al-Bashir (April 2019) after 30 years; transitional government formed.
HIPC decision point reached (2021), promising debt relief; then the October 2021 military coup froze the process.
War erupted between the army (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (April 2023), creating the world's largest displacement crisis.
War-driven hyperinflation (185.7% in 2024); economy collapsed; GDP in USD terms fell below $40bn.

outlook_next_decade: There is no meaningful economic outlook while the war continues: Sudan's economy has collapsed, inflation is near 100-200%, and debt at 188% of GDP is unserviceable. The base case is continued catastrophe. Upside exists only in a peace scenario, which would unlock HIPC completion and reconstruction; downside is state fragmentation. Uncertainty is total, and any projection is conditional on a political settlement that is not in sight.
